summary: During the California Gold Rush, rival armed gangs and a monopolistic egg company fought for decades over harvesting seabird eggs on the Farallon Islands, clashing with lighthouse keepers and devastating the murre colony.

evidence.note: Gold discovered at Coloma in 1848, triggering the San Francisco boom and egg shortage
Doc Robinson's first Farallon egg run in spring 1849
Six men claim the islands and incorporate an egg company
Dangerous work, deaths logged as missing, immigrant and blacklisted labor organizers as eggers
Head keeper Amos Clift hired in 1858 and tries to seize the egg trade
1863 gun battle between Batchelder's Italian fishermen and company men
Company turns to rendering sea lions and seals for oil as egg yields fall
Army evicts the egg company from the islands in 1881
Murre population collapses from about 400,000 to 60,000

notes: Primary subject is an event, so roles are empty. No theme for frontier resource wars; corporate-malfeasance chosen for the egg company's armed monopoly, with environmental-destruction a close alternative as primary. Clift's dates are not given; floruit set to his 1858 hiring.
